result.title: Automated Multi-Agent Organization Design: From Architecture Search to Organizational Learning
result.summary: Agentic system design is increasingly shifting from hand-crafted prompts and workflows toward automated search over agentic programs and interaction structures, with multi-agent systems receiving growing attention. Yet a central question remains unresolved: when does an automatically generated multi-agent structure exhibit a functionally meaningful division of responsibility? We argue that automated multi-agent design should move beyond searching for effective architectures toward identifying which responsibilities are functionally necessary, how they should be allocated, and when they should change. To explore this, we propose Automated Multi-Agent Organization Design (AMOD), which treats organization itself as a first-class design object, explicitly modeling how agent teams are composed, what functional responsibilities the agents assume, how they coordinate, and how collective decisions are made. We formulate AMOD as an execution-driven design loop. For each task, an automated designer instantiates an organization by assigning functional responsibilities and coordination rules to a set of agents. After execution, task outcomes, intermediate artifacts, and interaction traces are examined to identify which responsibilities may be missing, duplicated, or ineffective, and the organization is revised accordingly. We also propose testing discovered responsibilities by removing them, replacing them with generic roles, or changing their assignment under matched resource budgets, with complementary evaluations. AMOD provides a principled foundation for evidence-based and adaptive multi-agent organization design.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 AMOD，把多智能体「组织」本身作为设计对象，显式建模团队构成、功能职责分配、协调规则与集体决策；以执行驱动的设计循环，依据任务结果、中间产物和交互轨迹诊断职责缺失、重复或无效并迭代修订，并用删除职责、换成通用角色、等资源预算下改派等干预方式检验所发现职责的必要性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其基于干预的职责必要性检验（删除、替换、等预算改派）可供核查是否能迁移到 latent 推理步骤或状态的因果贡献分配与冗余判断；但论文不做视觉或多模态推理，也无内部表示层面的分析，联系仅限方法线索。
